reading_summary: Fixture fallback summary for a VisDoM-style multimodal document retrieval dataset. The retained papers emphasize layout-aware vision-language encoders, strong dual-encoder baselines, late-interaction retrieval, and hard-negative training for page-level recall.

sources.title: LayoutLMv3: Pre-training for Document AI with Unified Text and Image Masking
sources.abstract: LayoutLMv3 unifies text and image masking for document understanding and serves as a strong layout-aware baseline for visually rich document tasks.

sources.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
sources.abstract: ColBERT is a strong late-interaction retrieval baseline that improves recall while preserving token-level matching signals.

sources.title: DocFormer: End-to-End Transformer for Document Understanding
sources.abstract: DocFormer combines visual, textual, and spatial cues for document representation and is relevant for page-level document retrieval pipelines.

sources.title: CLIP: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
sources.abstract: CLIP provides a simple but strong dual-encoder baseline for image-text retrieval and often anchors multimodal retrieval comparisons.

reader_context.task_definition: Rank document pages so that the correct evidence page is retrieved early for a visually rich document query.
dataset_specific_challenges: Page-level supervision can hide fine-grained evidence mismatch inside long visual documents.
OCR noise, dense layouts, and tables often weaken text-only retrieval baselines.
Hard negatives may be visually similar pages from the same document or collection.
relevant_methods_landscape: Layout-aware document encoders such as LayoutLMv3 and DocFormer remain strong representation baselines.
Dual-encoder retrieval offers efficient first-stage recall, while late interaction improves difficult ranking cases.
Contrastive training with hard negatives is repeatedly used to raise retrieval recall without changing downstream generation.
likely_strong_baselines: OCR-text BM25 or dense text retrieval over page transcriptions.
CLIP-like dual-encoder retrieval with page image and query text embeddings.
Layout-aware document encoder plus contrastive retrieval head.
Late-interaction reranking on top of a dual-encoder shortlist.
common_failure_points: Retriever overweights repeated headers or boilerplate instead of evidence-bearing regions.
Visual-only cues dominate when OCR text is sparse or noisy.
Negative sampling is too easy, so recall collapses on near-duplicate pages.
evaluation_caveats: Official recall metrics can look healthy even when the exact evidence region is not localized.
Train/validation/test splits should be checked for document overlap and template leakage.
Page-level metrics should be interpreted before any snippet-level extension.
implementation_constraints: Need reusable page adapter and image-text batching that fits GPU memory.
Must preserve stable page ids and split definitions for reproducible recall evaluation.
Image resolution and OCR preprocessing choices can materially change retrieval quality.
promising_research_directions: Layout-aware hard-negative mining for visually similar but semantically wrong pages.
Two-stage retrieval with efficient page recall followed by region-sensitive reranking.
Query-conditioned page chunking or evidence-aware page representations.
